evidence: Receiving DO2 11.5 mg/L at 48.0 h → 4.40 mg/L at 48.2 h → 3.27 mg/L at 52.0 h (public observations), vs source batches never below ~7.4 mg/L
Model estimate: oxygen transfer multiplier fell to ~0.495 around 48 h

Forward model: strong_feed_reduction min DO 1.66 mg/L, deficit 0.52 mg·h/L, product mass 203.5 kg — best of all actions; keep min DO 1.40/175 kg; increase_air min DO 1.23; combined 1.48/181 kg; reduce_feed 1.26/176 kg
Sensitivity: strong_feed_reduction min-DO range 1.14–2.65 mg/L, 1/5 members feasible — most favorable among actions
P at 48 h = 3.27 g/L, on-trend vs source batches (~3.0 g/L), supporting continuation rather than stop
args.rationale: DO2 collapsed at ~48 h (transfer fault) and is drifting toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum. Bounded comparison of forward-model outcomes shows strong feed reduction (×0.6 feed, ×1.15 air) gives the smallest oxygen-constraint violation (min DO ~1.66 mg/L, lowest deficit) while retaining the highest product mass (~203 kg), far better than keep or air increase alone; stop is rejected as it yields zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; predicted post-action minimum DO spans ~1.14–2.65 mg/L across sensitivity members, so the oxygen floor may still be breached despite intervention. Magnitude/timing of the transfer fault is inferred only from public DO2 observations.
